questions.question: Which of the following epics is written by the Tamil poet, Ilango Adigal?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about solids is INCORRECT?

options.text: A solid has definite size and shape which do not change on their own.
In solids, the constituent particles are present very close to each other
Intermolecular forces operating between the constituent particles of a solid are very strong and capable of keeping the molecules in fixed positions.
When a solid is heated, the thermal energy of its particles decreases thereby converting it into liquid.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When a solid is heated, the thermal energy of its particles decreases thereby converting it into liquid. **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A solid has a definite size and shape which do not change on their own.

 
 
• This statement is **correct**. Solids have a rigid structure where the constituent particles are tightly packed, ensuring a fixed size and shape. Examples include a block of wood or a piece of metal.
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** In solids, the constituent particles are present very close to each other.
 
 
• This statement is **correct**. Solids exhibit a compact structure because their particles are tightly packed due to strong intermolecular forces. This arrangement contributes to their rigidity and incompressibility.
 
 
 
• **Statement 3:** Intermolecular forces operating between the constituent particles of a solid are very strong and capable of keeping the molecules in fixed positions.
 
 
• This statement is **correct**. Strong intermolecular forces in solids ensure that the particles remain in fixed positions within a lattice structure, giving solids their stability and resistance to deformation.
 
 
 
• **Statement 4:** When a solid is heated, the thermal energy of its particles decreases thereby converting it into liquid.
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**. When a solid is heated, the thermal energy of its particles **increases**, causing them to vibrate more vigorously. Eventually, the intermolecular forces weaken, leading to the melting of the solid into a liquid. Thus, the thermal energy increases, not decreases.
 
 
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of solids:**

 
 
• **Rigidity:** Solids maintain their shape and size due to strong intermolecular forces.
 
• **Definite volume:** Solids do not expand or compress easily, maintaining a fixed volume under normal conditions.
 
• **Incompressibility:** Solids cannot be compressed significantly due to the close packing of particles.
 
• **Melting point:** Solids have a specific melting point, depending on the strength of intermolecular forces.
 
 
 
• **Phase transition from solid to liquid:**
 
 
• When solids are heated, their particles gain **thermal energy**, increasing their kinetic energy.
 
• The increased energy overcomes the strong intermolecular forces, allowing particles to move freely, resulting in a liquid state.
 
• This process is called **melting**, and the temperature at which it occurs is known as the **melting point**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of solids:**
 
 
• **Crystalline solids:** Diamonds, salt, and metals exhibit a highly ordered structure.
 
• **Amorphous solids:** Glass and plastics lack a regular arrangement of particles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thermal energy and phase transition:**

 
 
• Thermal energy refers to the kinetic energy of particles due to heat.
 
• When solids absorb heat, their particles vibrate more vigorously, leading to an increase in thermal energy and eventual phase change.
 
• The melting process requires sufficient energy to overcome intermolecular forces, transitioning the substance into a liquid state.
 
 
 
• **Applications of solids:**
 
 
• Solids are used in construction (e.g., steel and cement) due to their rigidity and strength.
 
• Crystalline solids like diamonds are used in jewelry, while amorphous solids like glass are used in windows and optics.

questions.question: Banawali is an archaeological site in the state of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banawali** is an important **archaeological site** situated in the state of **Haryana**, India.
 
• It is located in the district of **Fatehabad**, Haryana, and is associated with the **Indus Valley Civilization**, which dates back to the period of approximately 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE.
 
• The site was excavated under the guidance of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, revealing significant evidence of the **Harappan culture**. *Hence, Haryana is the correct answer.*
 
• Banawali is notable for its distinct **rectangular layout**, fortified settlement patterns, and artifacts that depict the advanced urban planning and craftsmanship of the Harappan Civilization.
 
• The excavations at Banawali have uncovered items such as **terracotta figurines**, **beads**, **pottery**, and **tools**, which provide insights into the **daily life** and **economic activities** of the people who lived there.
 
• This site is one of the key locations that demonstrate the **transition** from rural to urban settlements in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Banawali holds immense importance in understanding the **spread** and **development** of Harappan culture across northern India. *Hence, Haryana is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization:**
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**, also known as the **Harappan Civilization**, was one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, flourishing around 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE.
 
• It was characterized by **advanced town planning**, including drainage systems, granaries, and organized streets.
 
• Major sites of the civilization include **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-Daro**, **Banawali**, **Rakhigarhi**, and **Lothal**.
 
 
 
• **Banawali Archaeological Site:**
 
 
• **Location:** Banawali is situated in the Fatehabad district of Haryana.
 
• **Excavations:** The site was excavated by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** under R.S. Bisht.
 
• **Findings:** Discoveries include **terracotta figurines**, **pottery**, **tools**, and **beads**, which depict the lifestyle and trade practices of the Harappan people.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• The Harappan sites exhibit **urban planning** with well-organized streets and drainage systems.
 
• Artifacts such as seals, ornaments, and terracotta toys highlight the **artistic skills** of the Harappan people.
 
• **Trade:** Evidence of trade relations with Mesopotamia and other regions has been found.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Major Harappan Sites:**
 
 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:** Located in present-day Pakistan, Mohenjo-Daro is known for its Great Bath and advanced drainage system.
 
• **Harappa:** Another significant site in Pakistan, Harappa revealed granaries and seals used for trade.
 
• **Rakhigarhi:** Situated in Haryana, Rakhigarhi is one of the largest Harappan sites discovered.
 
• **Lothal:** Located in Gujarat, Lothal is famous for its dockyard and evidence of maritime trade.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Banawali:**
 
 
• Banawali is unique because of its rectangular layout, which differs from other Harappan sites that were mostly grid-based.
 
• The site provides insights into the transition from rural to urban settlements in the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Its location in Haryana highlights the geographical spread of the Harappan culture into northern India.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: The Swaraj Party was formed in 1923 with ______ as its Secretary.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motilal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Swaraj Party** was established in the year **1923** by prominent leaders **Motilal Nehru** and **Chittaranjan Das** to express their dissatisfaction with the policies and methods of the Indian National Congress, particularly after the suspension of the **Non-Cooperation Movement**.
 
• Its primary objective was to enter the legislative councils and obstruct or influence British policies from within, rather than boycotting the councils entirely.
 
• **Motilal Nehru** served as the **Secretary** of the Swaraj Party, while **Chittaranjan Das** became its **President**. This leadership division was essential in organizing the party's activities and strategies effectively. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The Swaraj Party aimed at achieving **‘Swaraj’** (self-governance) through constitutional means, unlike the revolutionary or extremist groups that sought immediate independence through more aggressive measures.
 
• Their goal was to use their presence in legislative councils to expose the flaws of British administration, demand reforms, and press for greater autonomy for Indians. *Hence, the correct answer is Motilal Nehru.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Context Behind the Formation of Swaraj Party:**

 
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement**, launched by **Mahatma Gandhi** in 1920, came to an abrupt end in 1922 after the **Chauri Chaura incident**, where a violent clash resulted in the death of several policemen. This led to disillusionment among many leaders.
 
• Leaders like **Motilal Nehru** and **Chittaranjan Das**, who were moderate in approach, believed in working within the system rather than boycotting it entirely.
 
• The Swaraj Party was thus formed to act as an opposition within the councils and push for reforms and self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Main Objectives of the Swaraj Party:**
 
 
• **Legislative Obstruction:** To enter the councils and obstruct the functioning of colonial government policies that were detrimental to Indian interests.
 
• **Demand Reforms:** To press for constitutional reforms, such as greater representation for Indians in governance.
 
• **Expose British Policies:** To use their presence in councils as a platform to expose the exploitative nature of British rule.
 
 
 
• **Role of Swaraj Party Leaders:**
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru:** As the Secretary, he played a pivotal role in formulating the party’s strategies and organizing its activities in legislative councils.
 
• **Chittaranjan Das:** As the President, he provided the ideological foundation and leadership for the party.
 
 
 
• **Outcome of the Swaraj Party:**
 
 
• The Swaraj Party succeeded in gaining a significant number of seats in the 1923 elections to the legislative councils.
 
• It used its presence to highlight the inadequacies of British administration and demand reforms.
 
• However, the party gradually lost momentum after the death of **Chittaranjan Das** in 1925 and due to internal differences.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Motilal Nehru:** A senior Congress leader, lawyer, and politician, Motilal Nehru played a crucial role in the Indian freedom struggle and later became a prominent member of the Swaraj Party.
 
• **Chittaranjan Das:** Known as **‘Deshbandhu’** (Friend of the Nation), he was a prominent nationalist leader, lawyer, and the first President of the Swaraj Party.
 
• **Legacy:** The Swaraj Party laid the groundwork for future political movements and was instrumental in bringing constitutional reforms to the forefront of the freedom struggle.

__
 
• **Vitamin C** is a **water-soluble vitamin**. It dissolves in water and is easily absorbed by the body.
 
• Water-soluble vitamins, such as Vitamin C, are not stored in the body for long periods. Instead, they are excreted through urine, requiring regular replenishment through diet.
 
• **Vitamin C** is essential for **collagen synthesis**, which helps in wound healing, tissue repair, and maintaining skin elasticity. *Hence, Vitamin C is classified as water-soluble.*
 
• **Sources of Vitamin C** include **citrus fruits** (like oranges and lemons), **berries, kiwis, bell peppers, broccoli**, and **leafy greens**.

• The other options — **Vitamin A, Vitamin K, and Vitamin E** — are **fat-soluble vitamins**. These are stored in the body's fatty tissues and liver for longer periods and do not dissolve in water. *Hence, these statements are incorrect.*

• **Fat-soluble vitamins:**
 
 
• Fat-soluble vitamins include **Vitamin A, Vitamin D, Vitamin E, and Vitamin K**. These require dietary fat for absorption and are stored in the liver and fatty tissues.
 
• Fat-soluble vitamins play crucial roles, such as **immune support**, **vision**, **bone health**, and **blood clotting**.

• **Applications:** Vitamin C is commonly used in **dietary supplements**, skincare products, and treatments for common colds and immunity boosting.

• **Key Characteristics of Water-Soluble Vitamins:**

 
 
• Water-soluble vitamins are not stored in the body, and excess amounts are excreted through urine. Hence, they must be consumed regularly through diet.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-communicable disease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Epilepsy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-communicable diseases (NCDs):** These are medical conditions or diseases that are not caused by infectious agents. Instead, they are chronic diseases that progress slowly and are usually the result of genetic, physiological, environmental, and behavioral factors.
 
• **Epilepsy:** It is a **neurological disorder** characterized by recurrent seizures, which are sudden bursts of electrical activity in the brain. It is classified as a non-communicable disease because it is not infectious or transmissible from one person to another.
 
• Conditions like epilepsy are influenced by **genetic predisposition, brain injury, or developmental disorders**, not by pathogens. Hence, it is considered a non-communicable disease.
 
• **Other options:** Cholera, tuberculosis, and smallpox are all communicable diseases caused by infectious agents and can be transmitted between individuals. Hence, they do not fall under the category of non-communicable diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Details of each option:**

 
 
• **Cholera:** This is a **communicable disease** caused by the bacterium **Vibrio cholerae**. It spreads through contaminated water and food and leads to acute diarrheal illness. Cholera is common in areas with poor sanitation and limited access to clean drinking water.
 
• **Epilepsy:** This is a **chronic, non-communicable neurological disorder**. It can occur due to brain damage, genetic factors, or unknown causes. Seizures in epilepsy may vary in severity, and treatment often involves anti-epileptic medication or surgery in severe cases.
 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):** This is a **communicable disease** caused by the bacterium **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**. It primarily affects the lungs but can also spread to other parts of the body. TB spreads through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.
 
• **Smallpox:** This was a highly contagious disease caused by the **variola virus**. It caused severe rash and fever, leading to significant mortality. However, **smallpox was eradicated globally in 1980** through widespread vaccination efforts.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Non-Communicable Diseases:**
 
 
• NCDs are not caused by infectious agents and cannot be passed from person to person.
 
• Common types of NCDs include **cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes, chronic respiratory diseases, and neurological disorders** like epilepsy.
 
• Risk factors for NCDs include **genetic predisposition, unhealthy diet, lack of physical activity, tobacco use, and alcohol consumption**.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact:**

• In cases where medication is ineffective, **surgical procedures, ketogenic diets, or other therapies** may be considered.
 
• Preventive measures include **reducing head injuries, improving maternal and neonatal care, and controlling infections** that may lead to epilepsy.
 
 
 
• **Public Awareness:**
 
 
• **Stigma** associated with epilepsy is a significant challenge. Public education and awareness campaigns can help reduce misconceptions and discrimination against individuals with epilepsy.
 
• The **International Epilepsy Day**, observed annually on the second Monday of February, aims to raise awareness and provide support to people with epilepsy.

• Rudradaman ruled over a vast territory covering parts of present-day **Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh**. This highlights the geographical extent of his empire.
 
• He is credited with the repair of the **Sudarshana Lake**, an ancient reservoir in Gujarat, showcasing his administrative efficiency and focus on public works.
 
• **Rudradaman’s Junagarh Rock Inscription** is one of the earliest inscriptions written in classical Sanskrit. It highlights his achievements and his proficiency in Sanskrit.
 
• He was a follower of **Hinduism**, but he also showed tolerance towards other religions, reflecting the cultural diversity of his time.
 
• The Shaka dynasty originated from the **Scythians**, who migrated to India, and they are known for their contributions to Indian culture, governance, and architecture.

• They ruled large parts of western and central India and played a crucial role in shaping the political and cultural landscape of the region.
 
 
 
• **Junagarh Rock Inscription:**
 
 
• The Junagarh Rock Inscription of Rudradaman is one of the most important historical records, written in **150 CE**.
 
• This inscription is significant because it is one of the earliest examples of **classical Sanskrit** and provides detailed information about Rudradaman's reign.
 
• It mentions the repair of the Sudarshana Lake in **Saurashtra**, highlighting his focus on public welfare and infrastructure development.

• **Sunga Dynasty:** The Sunga dynasty ruled after the fall of the Mauryan Empire in northern India. They do not have any direct association with Rudradaman or the Shaka dynasty.

• He maintained peace and stability in his empire and promoted trade and commerce, which significantly contributed to the prosperity of his kingdom.
